title: Partnership in crime, incubated behind bars in Telangana

title: ‘Hypnotised’ with water, raped: Mumbai airhostess falls prey to 'evil eye’ ploy
content: A 25-year-old airhostess was allegedly raped by a man posing as transgender. The accused entered her flat on the pretext of using black magic for her husband. Police arrested the 28-year-old accused within four hours of the FIR being registered. His movements were traced using footage from over one hundred CCTV cameras. The accused faces charges including rape and criminal intimidation.

title: India, Nepal to drone-map 'Dasgaja' encroachments after Balen remark row
content: In a significant move towards resolving land disputes, India and Nepal will utilize drones to meticulously map border encroachments in the Dasgaja regions. This collaborative effort will provide a verified technical account of disputed areas, facilitating future discussions on land restoration and compensation. By addressing cross-border land occupation, the initiative aims to mitigate long-standing issues and deter minor conflicts from escalating.

title: Rajya Sabha member's son in soup after Aston Martin crash kills woman in Hyderabad
content: Madhapur police booked Lingamaneni Sanjush, son of MP Lingamaneni Ramesh, for rash driving. His Aston Martin allegedly killed a 26-year-old mall employee near Inorbit Mall on August 16. The victim, Bharati Mukhi, was crossing the road when the speeding car hit her severely. Sanjush, who tested negative for alcohol and drugs, rushed her to the hospital. Police registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for causing death by negligence.

title: Financial loss, betting, corruption: BCB suspends Bangladesh Premier League
content: The BPL began in 2012 and is Bangladesh’s biggest domestic cricket tournament. However, it has struggled to match the success of other franchise leagues such as IPL.

title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna on letter that sent stock down 25%, ‘worst day’ in history
content: The CEO of IBM took the bold step of revealing a financial deficit to stakeholders, triggering a notable decline in stock prices. This transparency caused clients to halt infrastructure advancements in favor of buying data center hardware. Krishna noted that distractions from rising AI trends and supply limitations were crucial factors. He is convinced that promptly revealing issues enables a sharper focus on strategic remedies.

title: Middle East oil squeeze: How much crude is actually flowing through Hormuz
content: US officials assert that oil is moving through the Strait of Hormuz at a pace far exceeding market projections. External data indicates a drop in oil tanker activity and a decline in global stockpiles. This divergence raises questions about the true amount of crude oil flowing into worldwide markets. Additionally, shadow fleets attempting to mask their locations complicate monitoring efforts, leading to potential volatility in oil prices and supply predictions.

title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
content: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk turned Meta software engineer, inadvertently initiated FSH Technologies during a hackathon held in the pandemic. Teaming up with friends, they transformed their project into a burgeoning company, now ready to rival traditional government contractors. With her unique insights, Chen has revolutionized the company's consulting style to emphasize holistic system solutions over piecemeal projects.

title: Jaipur resort told to refund 85% of Rs 10 lakh after wedding cancelled
content: A consumer commission ordered a Jaipur resort to refund Rs 8.5 lakh for a cancelled wedding.  The resort could not keep the entire Rs 10 lakh advance payment.  The commission found the resort failed to prove actual losses from the cancellation.  It allowed the resort to retain Rs 1.5 lakh for booking expenses.  The order directed the refund within forty-five days.

title: After 28 years, Tasmania declares invasive carp functionally eradicated
content: After a remarkable 28-year campaign, Tasmania's fisheries service has successfully eliminated invasive common carp from Lake Sorell and Lake Crescent. This effort has seen the removal of over 49,000 harmful fish, leading to clearer waters and the revival of native plant life in marsh areas. The resurgence of wild brown trout has also enhanced recreational fishing opportunities for anglers, proving that large lakes can recover from invasive species.

title: Reindeer released for food on South Georgia later damaged native vegetation
content: In 1911, reindeer were introduced to South Georgia by Norwegian whalers. This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear.

title: America’s top VC tells Altman & Amodei: You have failed miserably
content: Chamath Palihapitiya has issued a caution to leaders in the AI sector regarding increasing public backlash towards data centers. He highlights the precarious nature of the tech industry, noting that political campaigns are leveraging data centers as vulnerabilities. Palihapitiya urges industry heads to effectively share the advantages of AI and its value to communities, while also advocating for the cessation of internal disputes and resisting governmental meddling.

title: Why the US is deporting migrants to Liberia instead of their home countries
content: The United States deported twenty non-Liberian nationals to Liberia. This marks a significant expansion of the US third-country deportation program. Liberia agreed to accept up to twelve hundred individuals under this humanitarian arrangement. The agreement allows deportees to seek asylum within Liberia if they wish. This policy aims to manage immigration and strengthen border security.

The film's first week ended with Rs 41.90 crore, and its second week reached Rs 19.64 crore. DC's domestic gross collection stands at Rs 70.85 crore, with overseas earnings at Rs 21.85 crore.

title: Visakhapatnam UKG student dies after teacher slaps him for incomplete homework
content: A five-year-old UKG student died after an alleged teacher slap at a Visakhapatnam private school. The boy's parents allege the teacher assaulted him for incomplete homework, leading to his death. CCTV footage reportedly shows the teacher slapping the child after he showed an empty slate. The school informed the parents much later, sparking protests and an official investigation.

title: 'Pakistan a poor side': Former England great delivers blunt verdict
content: Stuart Broad called Pakistan a poor side and expects England to win the series. Pakistan's batting struggled, being bowled out for 171 on the first day. England then took a significant first-innings lead of 195 runs. Several England batters scored half-centuries, with Harry Brook narrowly missing a century. Broad's comments add pressure on Pakistan to recover in the ongoing contest.

title: After Rana’s demise, Oly medallist Manu forging new bonds with Serbian coach
content: Paris Olympics double medallist Manu Bhaker is showing a more flexible approach as she prepares for the 2028 Los Angeles Games. After coach Jaspal Rana’s sudden death, Bhaker has adapted to Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic’s methods, spending over eight hours training daily. Jelena says Bhaker’s openness to new ideas reflects her hunger to improve, with the 24-year-old focused on becoming better and more consistent.

title: At least 10 injured after crane falls on railway OHE in Mumbai’s Kurla
content: A crane from an MMRDA work site fell onto railway equipment early Friday. Ten people sustained injuries in the incident near Qureshi Nagar in Kurla. The overhead equipment on the Kurla-Trombay section was damaged by the falling crane. Train movement was not affected as the section primarily handles goods traffic. Central Railway stated MMRDA is responsible for the crane collapse.

title: 'Genuinely cleaner and safer': Foreign tourists praise Delhi Metro
content: Two international visitors took to Instagram to share their delightful experiences with the Delhi Metro, praising its cleanliness and impressive security measures at various stations. They particularly adored the women-only coach, finding it a comforting choice, especially during peak hours. Their posts ignited conversations around safety and amenities in public transportation, highlighting the importance of such features in enhancing traveler comfort.

title: Teen driving car with booze consignment kills pedestrian near Mumbai
content: A 16-year-old boy allegedly driving a car with liquor ran over two women pedestrians. One woman died from her injuries while the other sustained serious harm. The vehicle's owner and registered driver were also booked by the police. The deceased woman's husband alleged common issues of illegal liquor transport and underage driving. Locals gathered demanding strict action against those responsible for the incident.

title: US vows toughest-ever Iran sanctions, presses China to help reopen Hormuz
content: The United States is preparing unprecedented sanctions against Iran. These measures aim to increase economic pressure on Tehran significantly. Washington also seeks cooperation from China regarding Iranian oil trade. China rejects sanctions and advocates for diplomatic solutions to the conflict. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical point in this ongoing dispute.

title: 'Multiple things' led to Deepika's exit: Sandeep Reddy's brother on 'Spirit' controversy
content: Sandeep Reddy Vanga's brother has revived controversy regarding Deepika Padukone's exit from 'Spirit'.  He cited remuneration and scheduling as primary reasons for her departure from the film.  Padukone reportedly demanded ten percent of the film's profit, which was deemed unfeasible.  Discussions about the story and character were also allegedly leaked by the actress.  The makers claimed they were willing to pay more but economics did not align.

title: Joe Root scripts history, becomes first player to achieve this feat
content: In a groundbreaking achievement, Joe Root has scored 3,000 runs as captain in the World Test Championship, marking a historic moment during England's first Test against Pakistan at Headingley. Root's remarkable batting skills have firmly established him atop the WTC captaincy run charts. His stellar performance has not only propelled England to a commanding first-innings advantage but also reinforces his legacy in Test cricket.

title: England leave Pakistan on the ropes at Headingley after day 2
content: Joe Root, Harry Brook, Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence all scored half-centuries after England resumed from 112/2. Rain delayed the start of play by nearly four hours, but England's batters made the most of the time available.

title: Brent hovers near $94 as US-Iran conflict continues to squeeze energy supply
content: On Friday, oil prices held steady, with Brent crude nearing $94 per barrel amid ongoing supply disruptions triggered by the US-Iran conflict. Both Brent and WTI benchmarks are poised for a second consecutive weekly increase. President Trump earlier issued threats of retaliation against nations backing Iran, as the ongoing war has resulted in significant casualties and interruptions to oil and gas supplies.

title: 8-0 becomes 8-1: 'Impatient' PV Sindhu falls to cramping Wang Zhi Yi in epic duel

Ayush Shetty also bowed out, while Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Satwik-Chirag marched into the quarter-finals.

title: Brittany Mahomes builds $15 million business empire beyond Patrick Mahomes
content: Brittany Mahomes has built a career that extends well beyond her connection to Patrick Mahomes. After retiring from professional soccer in 2017, she became a certified fitness trainer and launched Brittany Lynne Fitness. She later joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Current, while expanding her profile through social media and brand partnerships. Her journey reflects how she turned athletic experience into opportunities across fitness, entrepreneurship and women's sports.

title: How a daycare field trip at age 6 changed Simone Biles’ life forever
content: Simone Biles’ extraordinary gymnastics journey began with an ordinary daycare field trip when she was just six. During a visit to a Houston gymnastics center, Biles copied the gymnasts she watched, catching a coach’s attention. The center later sent a letter home encouraging her to try gymnastics. That small invitation opened the door to a career that would eventually make Biles one of the greatest gymnasts in history.

title: How Rafael Nadal’s family and Uncle Toni shaped his tennis greatness
content: Rafael Nadal’s greatest lesson may sit beyond his 22 Grand Slam titles. From Uncle Toni’s strict training to the support of his parents, sister and wife Mery, family shaped the champion he became. Nadal always remained connected to Mallorca and wanted to be remembered as a good person. His story shows how discipline, gratitude and family can shape greatness.

title: 'Shocked': Kangana reacts to Sharmila Tagore's 'Vande Mataram' comment
content: The conversation surrounding the religious undertones of Vande Mataram has reignited. Esteemed actress Sharmila Tagore voiced her apprehensions regarding its acceptance by followers of monotheistic religions. In contrast, Kangana Ranaut interpreted the verses as powerful symbols, advocating for an inclusive understanding that transcends religious boundaries. This dialogue underscores the historical importance and national identity encapsulated in Vande Mataram.

title: 'U-turn in a week': DMK slams Vijay over delimitation stance after Shah meeting
content: the DMK accuses the chief minister of taking a 'U-turn' on the issue of delimitation . he met amit Shah in Tamil Nadu on the same week that a resolution was passed to not increase the current number of 543 MPs . the party says he has changed his position .

title: Scientists discover nearly 400 fossils in France revealing life near the South Pole
content: fossils belong to the newly described Cabrières Biota, an early Ordovician fossil site in the Montagne Noire that preserves both hard-bodied animals and delicate soft tissues . discovery is particularly important because most ancient fossil communities with soft-tissue preservation come from tropical or temperate regions .

title: 8 on board as twin-engine Cessna charter plane crashes in remote Alaska
content: Cessna charter plane crashed near a remote radar site in western Alaska . the twin-engine plane was flying from Anchorage to Cape Newenham . it was carrying two pilots and six passengers, the national transportation safety board says .

title: 6 Indians on board hijacked cargo ship carrying Turkish weapons off Somalia's coast
content: crew of 10 includes six Indian nationals, one Turkish national, one Georgian and two Serbian security guards . eight pirates believed to have seized the vessel off Somalia's Puntland coast earlier this week .

title: 'China will be India's main competitor': Ex-Army chief Naravane
content: MM Naravane described china as India's "main competitor" in the years ahead . he distinguished between the two, saying the focus on Pakistan was driven largely by the threat of terrorism . the former army chief said he had used the term "competitor" for china .

title: Express train kills 4 workers carrying out weed-control work on tracks in Japan
content: four workers killed after train hits track workers in japan . collision occurred at 10.46 am (local time) while workers were spraying herbicide on track . train services on the tobu Nikko Line suspended . four men, three workers and a supervisor, taken to hospital .

title: US envoy in Ladakh, may meet Dalai Lama in first trip since Galwan clash
content: the 91-year-old tibetan spiritual leader has been recuperating in ladakh since June 28 following a medical procedure on his left knee in new Delhi . there were reports that he was likely to meet the Dalai Lama during his two-day trip .

title: 'Freeze seats for 25 years': Congress backs Vijay-led TN govt's delimitation stand
content: former union minister and senior Congress leader said the party wants the existing allocation of Lok Sabha seats to be maintained for another 25 years . there should be no change to the current strength of 543 seats or Tamil Nadu’s 39 constituencies .

title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan returns to jail after medical examination at Islamabad hospital
content: 73-year-old cricket legend has been facing health issues after 3 years in prison . he was taken to hospital days after the Supreme Court ordered a medical examination . his family and friends had sought permission for him to remain in hospital .

title: Watch: Indian seafarers take cover as vessel attacked in Hormuz back in April
content: the FSUI released an old video showing a vessel carrying 22 crew members, including 21 Indians, coming under attack in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22 . the footage shows several small boats surrounding the vessel, an RPG being fired and seafarers rushing to the ship’s alleyways to take cover .
